scenes.line1: Why do browsers send extra requests?
scenes.say: Ever notice browsers making extra requests before your API call? Let's see why preflights matter.

scenes.label: CORS
scenes.sub: Controls which domains can access resources.
scenes.say: CORS, or Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, controls which domains can access your server's resources.

rows.b: Browser checks headers, then sends real request

scenes.say: When your request uses custom headers or methods, the browser sends an OPTIONS request first. This checks if the server allows it. If the headers match, the real request goes through.

scenes.title: Preflight Request & Response
scenes.say: Here's what a preflight looks like. The browser asks, and the server replies with allowed origins and methods.

scenes.question: How do you debug a CORS error?
scenes.wrong: Ignore the browser and check server logs.
scenes.right: Check the browser network tab and CORS headers in the response.
scenes.say: Don't just check server logs. Always use your browser's network tab and inspect the CORS headers to debug these issues.
